purpose: Checkpoint-selection fork pool: the retail DEV twin of the 34-point retail TEST fork benchmark in docs/reports/forks_tau2_retail_test.json (run_ids_sha 1a060380806fff3e), so a candidate inquirer_trained checkpoint can be screened on fork behaviour without opening the test fork set.

derivation.splitter: pinq.splitting.split_of('tau2_retail', task_id, template_id=None). Retail's template_id is always None (Tau2RetailSuite.template_id_for: 'a retail id is a bare integer with no composition to recover'), so the hash key is the bare task id: bucket('tau2_retail', task_id) = int(h('split','tau2_retail',task_id)[:8],16) % 100, with TRAIN_MAX=59, DEV_MAX=74 (0-59 train, 60-74 dev, 75-99 test). tau2_retail is not in FIXED_SPLITS (only tau2_airline is) and not in EVAL_ONLY_SUITES, so this hash is the whole rule -- tests/test_airline_fixed_split.py pins that FIXED_SPLITS == {'tau2_airline'}.
derivation.trace_sources: data/traces/tau2/as_*/retail.jsonl only (8 files: as_c45, as_c4o, as_ds32, as_gpt5, as_kimi, as_o3, as_o4m, as_qwen -- the AgentSuite/tau2-bench-trajectories release). Restricted to these because every one of the 32 distinct trace_sha behind the recorded 34-point TEST set (artifacts/prereg_draft/fork_points.tau2_retail.json) resolves to one of these 8 files (as_ds32 6, as_kimi 6, as_c45 5, as_o3 4, as_qwen 3, as_gpt5 3, as_o4m 3, as_c4o 2) and NONE to data/traces/tau2/{nablo_retail,cloudsurf_retail,uq_kimi_k25}/retail.jsonl, whose `dataset` field values are not a recognisable public frontier-model trajectory release. This restriction is moot in practice for the DEV points specifically: none of those three excluded files contain a single dev-task row. All 656 as_* retail rows carry reward==1.0 already -- the 'trajectory that succeeded' precondition the fork design requires -- so no further success filter was applied.
derivation.cut_rule: pi_run.stages.tau2_fork.fork_points(messages, env._is_mutating_tool, trace_sha=..., task_id=...), env = tau2.domains.retail.environment.get_environment() (the same object tool_retriever.py and actuator.py consult for the identical predicate). A point is offered at every k immediately after a plain user handover turn (text, no tool calls), strictly before the first mutating tool call by either participant; an unknown tool name counts as mutating. This is the same legality rule the 34 recorded TEST points satisfy.
derivation.informativeness_rule: pi_run.stages.tau2_fork.work_remains(messages, k): keeps a cut only if the source trace issues at least one more tool call after k, i.e. the prefix had not already finished the task. Judged on the source trace, never on a policy run, so it partitions fork points rather than selecting on an outcome.
derivation.depth_filter: None applied. scripts/run_tau2_forks.py's own --forkpoints pool path defaults to --min-k 8, but the 34 recorded TEST points include k as low as 2 (13 of 34 have k<8), so a min-k 8 floor would be a stricter, different rule than the one the test set was actually built with, not 'the same code path'.

pins_of_the_recorded_benchmark_this_mirr.note: inquirer_trained uses the identical drafter/answerer pins (pinq_expt.arms.ARMS['inquirer_trained']: 'the ONLY difference is the model pin') and differs from inquirer_prompted only in PI_MODEL_INQUIRER, which must be set to a checkpoint id registered in conf/checkpoints.json at launch -- deliberately not chosen here, since picking one is what checkpoint selection means. All four roles are resolved from PI_MODEL_DRAFTER / PI_MODEL_ANSWERER / PI_MODEL_INQUIRER / PI_MODEL_USERSIM at launch time (pinq_adapters/llm/litellm_client.py ROLE_ENV); none of them are a Grid or pool field.
